channel.title: VICEPULSE news
channel.description: Takedowns, leaks, legal news, scams and real progress on running GTA VI on PC.

item.title: Victory-4080Super reports around 40 rendered FPS in a two-minute GTA VI sample
item.description: The 4K readings came from one area during a 36-minute run. A separate Proton fork reports a 33 FPS mean in its own boat-mission test.

item.title: VIctory-reloaded reports 29.6 FPS in the cell as a longer Radeon run slows
item.description: The RTX 4090 test covered one prologue scene. VIctory-RDNA’s 37-minute 4K capture on an RX 7900 XT logged a 15.35 rendered FPS median.

item.title: AnyXboxX reports 24 FPS median in a GTA VI launcher test
item.description: The 14-minute run reached the 30 FPS cap in lighter scenes. Heavy scenes still fell to 10–18 FPS.

item.title: CBL VIctory and VIctory-RDNA document longer GTA VI PC runs
item.description: CBL reports a clean exit after 72 minutes of uptime on an RTX 5080. VIctory-RDNA logs a 20.8 rendered FPS median on an RX 7900 XT.

item.title: Vice-Tay and VI-BR-PORT approach 30 FPS in short GTA VI boat tests
item.description: Vice-Tay reports 26.72 rendered FPS at 4K output. VI-BR-PORT reports 28.7–29.1 FPS at 1080p on an 8 GB RTX 4060 Ti.

item.title: fxceless adopts VIctory-NVIDIA as a new release trades FPS for better lighting
item.description: One maintainer reports about 17 FPS in a 25-minute open-world run on an RTX 4070. The latest upstream release warns of lower FPS with the improved visuals.

item.title: SeriesX Emulator and Port of the Americas repositories go offline
item.description: Both GitHub addresses now return 404. VIctory-NVIDIA still leads the active Race at 90%.

item.title: VIctory-NVIDIA leads at 90% as a private GTA VI demo shows multiplayer
item.description: The public fork reports 26–30 rendered FPS in opening rooms. Belobug and AvatarManz are now archived, and the stability forecast is low confidence.

item.title: Belobug takes the GTA VI PC lead with a reported 22 FPS average
item.description: Belobug moves to 91.3% overall. A community test reports no crashes on an RX 9070 XT, with the session duration still unknown.

item.title: AvatarManz leads the public race and reports 22 FPS in a GTA VI city test
item.description: CGBJ leads overall at 89.6% in Private Builds. DexNom and Belobug follow AvatarManz in the public standings.

item.title: GTA VI PC tracker records a 25 FPS report for CGBJ
item.description: The CGBJ footage shows the boat mission. Its GitHub repository returns 404, while AvatarManz’s public AMD fork reports about 19 FPS in a city-street test.

item.title: AvatarManz opens AMD VIctory fork and reports 19–22 FPS on GTA VI’s boat mission
item.description: The maintainer reports a 41-minute session without a crash on an RX 7900 XTX. Heavy street scenes still drop to 6–10 FPS.

item.title: Private VIctory demo reportedly peaks at 24 FPS in GTA VI free roam
item.description: The demo streamed by darkworldhm was previously reported to peak at 18 FPS. Typical performance is still reported around 12–15 FPS.

item.title: Belobug reports faster AMD gameplay as ZETTROX’s repo goes offline
item.description: Belobug now reports 5–7 FPS in the world. A separate free-roam stream is attributed to darkworldhm, whose build author remains unknown.

item.title: DexNom publishes a ray-tracing benchmark for GTA VI’s City scene
item.description: The public AMD fork reports 1.03 FPS with experimental ray tracing enabled on an RX 7900 XTX.

item.title: Doomsday reports private-build progress as ScarlettCompat advances through startup
item.description: Community coverage puts Doomsday at 3–5 FPS. ScarlettCompat’s public boot notes document 587 resolved imports.

item.title: GTA VI PC clips show faster interiors, with heavier scenes still slower
item.description: A prison clip shared by Linux4real shows sampled readings around 10–12 FPS. The build author is unknown. The separate victory-perf fork publishes its own numbers.

item.title: Belobug’s AMD build renders GTA VI’s open world at 3–5 FPS
item.description: The Radeon fork shows textured streets, traffic, vegetation and water. Driving runs at about 3 FPS on an RX 9070 XT.

item.title: GTA VI PC builds report longer runs at 1–5 FPS
item.description: ZETTROX reports a 90-minute session. A contributor testing the AnyXboxX team’s VIctory fork reports finishing two missions.

item.title: Leonida V2 joins the Watchlist as ZETTROX opens its source
item.description: Leonida V2 reports a blank startup window. ZETTROX has published its code, and a community tracker reports a second build reaching “Gone Fishing.”

item.title: Private GTA VI PC build reportedly reaches Jason’s first mission
item.description: A community tracker credits ZETTROX with getting past Lucia’s prologue into “Gone Fishing” at about 2 FPS.

item.title: GitHub processes Take-Two’s takedown across Leonida’s fork network
item.description: GitHub says the notice was processed against a network of 3,007 repositories, including the original.

item.title: GTA VI PC tracker now scores rendering, frame rate and stability
item.description: The new leaderboard separates getting into the game from correct graphics, sustained 30 FPS and crash-free sessions.

item.title: GTA VI footage surfaces on a reported M5 Max MacBook
item.description: A 41-second clip shows GTA VI scenes on a laptop identified by the poster as an M5 Max. Character models and some textures are visible, though lighting and materials still look inconsistent.

item.title: omonkey reportedly reaches GTA VI’s prison scene at about 5 FPS
item.description: A community tracker reports character movement and partial shader rendering in a private Windows build. It also reports progress on Five Star Recomp.

item.title: GTA VI PC footage shows sunlight and working lamps
item.description: A new 17-second clip shows bright light on Lucia and visible ceiling lamps, while much of the room stays almost black. The exact build is unconfirmed.

item.title: The next GTA VI PC milestone is a crash-free session
item.description: VICEPULSE is watching for a documented 30-minute gameplay run after a fast jump from menus to the game world.

item.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world
item.description: A private build based on VIctory and XCL lets a player walk around and talk to NPCs, very slowly. A video shows the opening scenes in flat colours, without lighting.

item.title: Exclusive: XCL reports 30 fps in GTA VI but won't say if it's past the menus
item.description: The team refused to say more for fear of being nuked, but hinted to one of our members that it's working really well. Update: testers' reports now show it loading into the world.

item.title: TuxBox draws GTA VI's first screen as VIctory edges into the world
item.description: Overnight, a Linux-first layer showed GTA VI's player-selection prompt, VIctory reported a title card inside the game world, and two smaller projects got GTA VI's code running.
